<?php
$stdin = fopen('php://stdin', 'r');
$line = fgets($stdin);
$A = trim($line);
$A = (int)$A;

if ($A == 1) {
    echo 1;
    exit;
}

$N = $A - 1;
$divisors = [];
$limit = (int)sqrt($N);
for ($i = 1; $i <= $limit; $i++) {
    if ($N % $i == 0) {
        $divisors[] = $i;
        if ($i != $N / $i) {
            $divisors[] = $N / $i;
        }
    }
}
sort($divisors);

$m = count($divisors);
$adj = array_fill(0, $m, []);
$divMap = [];
for ($i = 0; $i < $m; $i++) {
    $divMap[$divisors[$i]] = $i;
}

for ($i = 0; $i < $m; $i++) {
    $d = $divisors[$i];
    if ($d <= 2) continue;
    $p = $d - 1;
    if ($p <= 1) continue;
    $isPP = false;
    $basePrime = 0;
    if ($p == 2) {
        $isPP = true;
        $basePrime = 2;
    } else {
        if ($p % 2 == 0) {
            $isPP = false;
        } else {
            $primeFlag = true;
            $sqrtP = (int)sqrt($p);
            for ($k = 3; $k <= $sqrtP; $k += 2) {
                if ($p % $k == 0) {
                    $primeFlag = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if ($primeFlag) {
                $isPP = true;
                $basePrime = $p;
            } else {
                $maxE = (int)(log($p) / log(2)) + 1;
                for ($e = 2; $e <= $maxE; $e++) {
                    $r = round(pow($p, 1.0 / $e));
                    for ($b = $r - 1; $b <= $r + 1; $b++) {
                        if ($b < 2) continue;
                        $val = 1;
                        $overflow = false;
                        for ($k = 0; $k < $e; $k++) {
                            $val *= $b;
                            if ($val > $p) {
                                $overflow = true;
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                        if (!$overflow && $val == $p) {
                            $primeB = true;
                            if ($b == 2) {
                                $primeB = true;
                            } elseif ($b % 2 == 0) {
                                $primeB = false;
                            } else {
                                $sqrtB = (int)sqrt($b);
                                for ($k = 3; $k <= $sqrtB; $k += 2) {
                                    if ($b % $k == 0) {
                                        $primeB = false;
                                        break;
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                            if ($primeB) {
                                $isPP = true;
                                $basePrime = $b;
                                break 2;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if ($isPP) {
        $adj[$i][] = $basePrime;
    }
}

$memo = [];
function dfs($idx, $usedMask, $divisors, $adj, $divMap, &$memo, $N) {
    if ($idx == 0) return 1;
    $key = $idx . ',' . $usedMask;
    if (isset($memo[$key])) return $memo[$key];
    
    if ($divisors[$idx] == 1) {
        return $memo[$key] = 1;
    }
    
    $total = 0;
    // Not take any factor for this divisor? We must match exactly, so we iterate possible factors.
    // We process divisors in descending order? Here idx corresponds to current divisor value.
    // Standard approach: iterate divisors of current value.
    // But we precomputed adj for each divisor.
    // We try to pick a prime power factor d from adj[idx] such that d divides divisors[idx] and prime not used.
    // Since we go by index, we need to ensure we don't reuse primes.
    // The state is (current divisor value, used primes).
    // We can do DP on divisors sorted ascending.
    // Let's change approach: recursive function f(i, rem, usedPrimes) where i is index in divisors array?
    // Better: standard divisor DP.
    return $memo[$key] = $total;
}

// The above DP is complex. Let's use the recursive search over valid prime power factors.

$validFactors = [];
$factorPrimes = [];
foreach ($divisors as $d) {
    if ($d <= 2) continue;
    $p = $d - 1;
    if ($p <= 1) continue;
    $isPP = false;
    $basePrime = 0;
    if ($p == 2) {
        $isPP = true;
        $basePrime = 2;
    } else {
        if ($p % 2 == 0) {
            // even > 2 not prime power
        } else {
            $primeFlag = true;
            $sqrtP = (int)sqrt($p);
            for ($k = 3; $k <= $sqrtP; $k += 2) {
                if ($p % $k == 0) {
                    $primeFlag = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if ($primeFlag) {
                $isPP = true;
                $basePrime = $p;
            } else {
                $maxE = (int)(log($p) / log(2)) + 1;
                for ($e = 2; $e <= $maxE; $e++) {
                    $r = round(pow($p, 1.0 / $e));
                    for ($b = $r - 1; $b <= $r + 1; $b++) {
                        if ($b < 2) continue;
                        $val = 1;
                        $overflow = false;
                        for ($k = 0; $k < $e; $k++) {
                            $val *= $b;
                            if ($val > $p) { $overflow = true; break; }
                        }
                        if (!$overflow && $val == $p) {
                            $primeB = true;
                            if ($b == 2) $primeB = true;
                            elseif ($b % 2 == 0) $primeB = false;
                            else {
                                $sqrtB = (int)sqrt($b);
                                for ($k = 3; $k <= $sqrtB; $k += 2) {
                                    if ($b % $k == 0) { $primeB = false; break; }
                                }
                            }
                            if ($primeB) {
                                $isPP = true;
                                $basePrime = $b;
                                break 2;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if ($isPP) {
        $validFactors[] = $d;
        $factorPrimes[] = $basePrime;
    }
}

$m = count($validFactors);
$memo = [];

function solveRec($rem, $startIdx, $validFactors, $factorPrimes, $divMap, &$memo) {
    if ($rem == 1) return 1;
    $key = $rem . ',' . $startIdx;
    if (isset($memo[$key])) return $memo[$key];
    
    $total = 0;
    for ($i = $startIdx; $i < count($validFactors); $i++) {
        $d = $validFactors[$i];
        if ($d > $rem) break;
        if ($rem % $d == 0) {
            $p = $factorPrimes[$i];
            // We need to ensure prime p is not used in the recursion path.
            // Since we don't track used primes in key, we must pass used primes or ensure disjointness by construction.
            // But different factors can have same prime? No, each factor corresponds to a unique prime power (sigma(p^e)).
            // Can two different prime powers have the same sigma? Yes, e.g., sigma(2)=3, sigma(4)=7, etc. But for a given prime p, sigma(p^e) are distinct.
            // However, different primes can yield same sigma value? e.g., sigma(2)=3, sigma(3)=4? No. sigma(p) = p+1. Different primes give different sigma.
            // For higher powers: sigma(p^e) = (p^{e+1}-1)/(p-1). Could sigma(p^e) = sigma(q^f) for p != q? Yes, e.g., sigma(2^4)=31, sigma(5^2)=31. So same divisor d can come from different primes.
            // Our validFactors list has entries for each (d, p). So same d can appear multiple times with different p.
            // In recursion, we must ensure we don't use the same prime p twice.
            // We need to track used primes. Since number of primes is small, we can use bitmask if we map primes to indices.
        }
    }
    return $memo[$key] = $total;
}

// Map primes to indices
$uniquePrimes = array_unique($factorPrimes);
$primeToIdx = [];
foreach ($uniquePrimes as $idx => $p) {
    $primeToIdx[$p] = $idx;
}
$numPrimes = count($uniquePrimes);

$memo = [];
function solveRec2($rem, $startIdx, $usedMask, $validFactors, $factorPrimes, $primeToIdx, &$memo) {
    if ($rem == 1) return 1;
    $key = $rem . ',' . $startIdx . ',' . $usedMask;
    if (isset($memo[$key])) return $memo[$key];
    
    $total = 0;
    $n = count($validFactors);
    for ($i = $startIdx; $i < $n; $i++) {
        $d = $validFactors[$i];
        if ($d > $rem) break;
        if ($rem % $d == 0) {
            $p = $factorPrimes[$i];
            $pIdx = $primeToIdx[$p];
            if (($usedMask & (1 << $pIdx)) == 0) {
                $total += solveRec2($rem / $d, $i + 1, $usedMask | (1 << $pIdx), $validFactors, $factorPrimes, $primeToIdx, $memo);
            }
        }
    }
    return $memo[$key] = $total;
}

$ans = solveRec2($N, 0, 0, $validFactors, $factorPrimes, $primeToIdx, $memo);
echo $ans;
?>

source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print the number of solutions of the equation J(x) = A.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The single line of the input contains a single integer A (1 ≤ A ≤ 1012).
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteRecord x|n means that number n divides number x. is defined as the largest positive integer that divides both a and b.In the first sample test the only suitable value of x is 2. Then J(2) = 1 + 2.In the second sample test the following values of x match:  x = 14, J(14) = 1 + 2 + 7 + 14 = 24  x = 15, J(15) = 1 + 3 + 5 + 15 = 24  x = 23, J(23) = 1 + 23 = 24
source_data.prob_desc_description: It's tough to be a superhero. And it's twice as tough to resist the supervillain who is cool at math. Suppose that you're an ordinary Batman in an ordinary city of Gotham. Your enemy Joker mined the building of the city administration and you only have several minutes to neutralize the charge. To do that you should enter the cancel code on the bomb control panel.However, that mad man decided to give you a hint. This morning the mayor found a playing card under his pillow. There was a line written on the card:The bomb has a note saying "J(x) = A", where A is some positive integer. You suspect that the cancel code is some integer x that meets the equation J(x) = A. Now in order to decide whether you should neutralize the bomb or run for your life, you've got to count how many distinct positive integers x meet this equation.
